title: Captured US Submarine Triggers Gulf Tension
seoTitle: US Submarine Captured in Gulf, Raising Tensions
subtitle: The incident in the Strait of Hormuz highlights growing reliance on autonomous technology
excerpt: Amid mutual attacks between the US and Iran, Iran claims to have captured an autonomous US submarine in the Strait of Hormuz as Washington responds.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A United States autonomous submarine was reportedly captured by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard, according to reports from the Iranian military body. The 19-foot (5.8-meter) vehicle was identified as a Dive-LD, developed by Anduril, and was allegedly intercepted at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz in a high-risk area for maritime navigation.

What changed in the Strait of Hormuz

Iran announced that the capture took place at an undisclosed location, but in images released by the state-run Fars agency, the submarine appears in a deep-water setting. The statement was made by the Revolutionary Guard, which described the vehicle as "one of the most modern, intelligent, and uncrewed vessels of the US military."

United States response

A Pentagon spokesperson stated that the underwater drone had "failed more than a day ago" and at the time was "conducting research in regional waters." The statement emphasized that the submersible was an older model, lacking sensitive equipment or classified sonars.

Characteristics of the Dive-LD

Anduril describes the Dive-LD as an autonomous system that can operate for up to 10 days without returning to base, with a maximum depth of 6,000 meters. Each unit costs about $2.5 million, according to DefenseScoop. The vehicle can execute mine detection missions, seafloor mapping, intelligence gathering, and underwater infrastructure inspection.

Impact on US-Iran relations

The episode occurs amid a series of reciprocal attacks between the two nations. In recent days, the United States destroyed several Iranian oil tankers in response to ballistic missile launches by Iran. The conflict has driven up the price of Brent crude, reflecting the tension in one of the world's most critical oil routes.

The future of autonomous technologies

The US military has been investing in uncrewed systems, both on the surface and subsurface, seeking to reduce costs and risks. The capture of the Dive-LD highlights the risk of losses in operations that depend on advanced technology, while the Pentagon's response emphasizes the prototype nature of the vehicles in use.

With information from CNBC, Military Times.
